blocking_findings.summary: materialize.py rewrote the three CRLF source files in text mode, removing every CR byte (2,651 in total). So v31 differs from v30 by more than changes.patch records, the parent_source/ preimages are not v30's bytes, and PLAN.md's 'Every other v30 byte is unchanged' is false. The conversion is semantically inert, but the version record is inexact.
blocking_findings.evidence: E=/Users/sun/tongbu/study/phdproject/vla/.pipeline/experiments/2026-09-26_newton_stair_reproduction. E/versions/v31/materialize.py:207 'before = path.read_text()', :212 'path.write_text(after)', :219 preimage.write_text(before), :220 changes.patch built from those text-mode strings; :224 checks only which files changed. CR counts v30 -> v31: src/plan_env/include/plan_env/grid_map.h 433 -> 0, src/plan_env/src/grid_map.cpp 1060 -> 0, src/bspline_opt/src/bspline_optimizer.cpp 1158 -> 0; planner_manager.cpp and scan_replan_fsm.cpp were already LF-only. parent_source sha256 differs from v30: bspline_optimizer.cpp e34fa3c9.. vs eadf278d.., grid_map.cpp 08a70bad.. vs 2588081b.., grid_map.h cf867d83.. vs 243af1f1... 'patch -p1 --dry-run < versions/v31/changes.patch' on scratch copies of the v30 files gives '1 out of 1 hunks failed' for grid_map.cpp and bspline_optimizer.cpp; after patching, grid_map.h, grid_map.cpp and bspline_optimizer.cpp still differ from the v31 bytes. The wrong claim is at PLAN.md:79. Why the conversion is inert: after CRLF->LF normalisation the v30->v31 diff is exactly the patch's added lines (+4 grid_map.h, +66 grid_map.cpp, +7 fsm, +4 manager, +2 optimizer, 0 removed), and the three files contain no raw string literals or backslash line continuations. v29 and v30 used the same code, but every file they edited was LF-only.
blocking_findings.why_blocking: PLAN.md makes a false byte-identity claim. The recorded patch and preimages do not reproduce v31 from v30, which breaks the project rule that each version records its exact difference from its frozen parent.
blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Option 1: re-materialize with byte-preserving I/O (read_bytes().decode() and write_bytes(), or open(..., newline='')), rebuild, and show install_sha256.json unchanged (a Release build without -g should give identical objects). Option 2: keep the bytes but correct PLAN.md:79 to record the CRLF->LF normalisation of the three files, write byte-exact parent_source copies, and add a materialize assertion that the CRLF-normalised diff equals the intended edits.

non_blocking_findings.summary: refreshSensorInputs drains sensor_pose before cloud. If a new scan pair arrives while the cloud loop runs, its cloud is taken without its pose and is applied with the previous scan's pose. Because cloud_is_world is false, cloudCallback transforms points with the last applied pose, so the whole scan is mis-registered: wrong raycast origin, wrong occupancy updates, and misplaced hits in the persistent reactive_nonterrain_history_. The window is small, since the cloud loop must outlast the pose-to-cloud delivery gap. v31's stamp sort also fixes a v30 backlog mispair: the round-robin executor, with queues [p_k+1] and [c_k], applies c_k with p_k+1.
non_blocking_findings.evidence: grid_map.cpp:948 (take_poses for sensor_pose) runs before :949-957 (cloud loop); :1011-1012 and :1035 'pt_world = sensor_r * pt_sensor + ray_pos'; E/versions/v31/building_planner.yaml:35 'cloud_is_world: false'. The bridge publishes the pose, then the raw cloud, then the planner cloud, all with one stamp (runtime_sources/bridge/lite3_sim_bridge/foxy_bridge_node.py:522, 542-543). The contract publishes every pair with identical stamps before the call, so C5 cannot exercise this race.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Drain clouds first, then sensor poses, then body poses (reverse publication order), or re-drain sensor_pose after the cloud loop.

non_blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap each take() and stamp conversion in a try/catch that logs and skips, mirroring take_and_do_error_handling.

non_blocking_findings.summary: PLAN.md bounds within-step ageing by one A* search (about 0.08 s sim). But a step between refresh sites can contain several searches with a 0.2 s wall budget each: the seed search plus one per collision segment in initControlPoints before the first rebound_round, and one per segment inside each round's check_collision_and_rebound. v30 logged 85 A* timeouts. After a refresh the pose margin is about 0.1 s minus the 5 ms pose period and delivery time, and one search takes 0.078-0.086 s sim at the observed sim/wall ratios of 0.39-0.43. Two searches in one step therefore exceed the pose gate and probably the scan gate. Stationary samples then read as occupied, because a NaN yaw returns 1, which yields 'robot is inside an obstacle' and failed rounds mid-attempt. Only final_check is guaranteed fresh.
non_blocking_findings.evidence: PLAN.md:150-154; planner_manager.cpp:130 -> :159 (seed AstarSearch) -> :247 (initControlPoints) -> bspline_optimizer.cpp:140-160 (A* per segment) -> :996 (first rebound_round); bspline_optimizer.cpp:802-806 (A* inside a round, via L-BFGS earlyExit); grid_map.h:419; motion_heading.h:15; audits/.../RESULT.md:247-256.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_fix: State this in PLAN.md's claim boundary. In the trial, log input ages at each rebound_round and final_check, not only above the logging thresholds.

non_blocking_findings.summary: The contract exercises only the first site of each callback (exec or safety), with every input pending before the call and sim time frozen during it. C5's equivalence holds by construction: each scan pair shares one stamp, counts are equal, and body poses write disjoint state. The 'applies nothing' checks rely on log lines that print only above 0.15 s and 0.05 s ages, though the digests cover C1 and C5. The inner sites, which target the mid-callback ageing that motivated v31, run only with empty queues before the physical trial. COMPONENT_RESULTS.md:101-105 discloses this.
non_blocking_findings.evidence: make_refresh_probe.py:63-85 (publish everything, sleep 300 ms, then call) and :68-71 (identical stamps for pose and cloud); analyze.py:90-91, 113; grid_map.cpp:977. The only sites logged in green are exec and safety.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Before the trial, add a case where a helper thread publishes pending inputs during a long execFSMCallback or reboundReplan. Assert refresh lines at route_walk, replan_start, rebound_round and final_check, and a digest equal to executor processing. Include a cloud whose pose arrives in a later batch.

non_blocking_findings.summary: Every freshness test treats a stamp ahead of now() as stale. now() comes from the /clock thread, while the refresh applies the newest data immediately before a decision. If the clock thread has not yet processed the /clock that precedes a just-taken body pose or scan, the decision sees stamp > now and yields a NaN heading or StaleInput, the very signatures v31 targets. The input_refresh log line prints only above its thresholds, and trial_signatures.py reports after-ages as median and max only, so negative ages would go unseen.
non_blocking_findings.evidence: plan_env/include/plan_env/reactive_collision.h:91-93, 131-133; motion_heading.h:15; known_lite3_trunk.h:15, 32; rclcpp node_options.hpp:406 (use_clock_thread_ true); building_planner.yaml:8 (use_sim_time: true); foxy_bridge_node.py:588-590 (clock published, then body pose); E/versions/v31/trial_signatures.py:45-51.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Have trial_signatures.py report the minimum after-age and the count of negative after-ages per site, and log whenever an after-age is negative.

non_blocking_findings.summary: The FSM's odom_pos_ and odom_vel_ are still updated only by the executor, while GridMap's body pose (which sets the trunk-waiver centre and the yaw of stationary samples) is refreshed at every site. The two can now differ by a whole planning callback; in v30 both body_pose subscriptions were served in the same wait cycle. This affects GEN_NEW_TRAJ start states, non-reference REPLAN starts, EMERGENCY_STOP holds placed at odom_pos_, and the odom_vel_ < 0.1 exit test. PLAN.md:160 notes only 'not refreshed', not this inconsistency.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Record the inconsistency as a residual risk, or refresh odom_sub_ at the same sites in a later version.

non_blocking_findings.summary: adjustGlobalTargetIfOccupied runs its final-point check and goal-neighbourhood A* before the refresh. When it is entered from p2bRouteCallback, which no refresh precedes, both can use stale inputs. The effect is conservative (a wasted search, and a frontier instead of the neighbour target), but it contradicts 'each collision-deciding step' in PLAN.md:1 and :40.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Move the refresh to the top of the function in a later version, or reword PLAN.md.
